facts.statement: Myriacanthus was an extinct genus of cartilaginous fish in the order Chimaeriformes.
facts.quote: Myriacanthus is an extinct genus of cartilaginous fish belonging to the order Chimaeriformes.

facts.statement: The genus was first named by Louis Agassiz in 1836 based on a fin spine found in Jurassic rocks at Lyme Regis, Dorset.
facts.quote: The genus was first named by Louis Agassiz in 1836 for a fin spine discovered from Jurassic period rocks of Lyme Regis, Dorset.

facts.statement: The specimen used for the genus was previously identified by Henry De la Beche in 1822.
facts.quote: This specimen had previously been identified in 1822 by Henry De la Beche.

facts.statement: Myriacanthus had an elongated snout and a head covered in armor plates.
facts.quote: Myriacanthus had an elongated rostrum and a head that was armor plated.

facts.statement: The head armor included spines extending backward from the jaw corners.
facts.quote: This armor included spines that extended backwards from the corners of the jaw.

facts.statement: A fused cartilage block called a synarcual supported the dorsal fin and spine, while rings formed the spinal column behind the head.
facts.quote: Behind the head was a fused block of cartilage termed a synarcual which supported a dorsal fin and fin spine, and a series of rings which formed the spinal column.

facts.statement: Based on the head and neck size, the total length of Myriacanthus was likely over 1 meter.
facts.quote: Based on the size of the head and neck region, the total length was likely over 1 m long.

facts.statement: Myriacanthus belongs to the family Myriacanthidae and the order Chimaeriformes.
facts.quote: Myriacanthus is a member of the family Myriacanthidae and the order Chimaeriformes.

facts.statement: Myriacanthus is the type genus of the family Myriacanthidae.
facts.quote: It is the type genus of its family.

facts.statement: Myriacanthus lived from the Rhaetian to the Sinemurian, between 205.7 and 192.9 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Rhaetian to Sinemurian (205.7 to 192.9 million years ago)
